title: A Label-free Technique for the Spatio-temporal Imaging of Single Cell Secretions
protocol: Choose 25 mm diameter glass coverslips with an approximate thickness of 170 µm as substrates for nanofabrication.
Immerse the coverslips in piranha solution (3:1 ratio of sulphuric acid and hydrogen peroxide) for at least 6 hr.
Wash the piranha soaked coverslip with copious amount of ultrapure 18.2 M deionized distilled water (DDW).
Deposit 10 nm chromium thin film on the coverslips by e-beam evaporation to avoid charge effects during the patterning and imaging of nanostructures.
Spin the first layer of bilayer resist consisting of ethyl lactate methyl methacrylate (MMA_EL6) copolymer at 2,000 rpm for 45 sec and then bake at 150 °C.
Spin the second layer of poly-methyl methacrylate (950PMMA_A2) at 3,000 rpm for 45 sec then bake at 180 °C.
Pattern the bilayer resist using the electron beam lithography (EBL) at 25 kV with an area dose of 300 µC/cm².
Develop in isopropyl alcohol (IPA)/methyl isobutyl ketone (MIBK): 2/1 and rinse in IPA.
Deposit Ti (5 nm) / Au (80 nm) film on the substrate using a e-beam evaporator.
Lift off the copolymer bilayer resist by soaking the substrate in acetone for 4 hr.
Inspect the substrate using the scanning electron microscope (SEM) to confirm nanostructure shape and size.
Remove remaining chromium from the substrate via wet etch using CR-7 etchant for 60 sec at room temperature.
Rinse in deionized water.
Design a center-to-center array spacing of 33 µm to leave room for cell imaging between arrays.
Pattern the nanostructures in a 20 x 20 pattern with a pitch of 300 nm using an e-beam writer.
Inspect a subset of arrays using the atomic force microscope (AFM) for verification of size and uniformity.
Attach a support ring to the back of the coverslip using UV curing epoxy.
Plasma ash at a power of 40 W in a 5% hydrogen, 95% argon mixture at 300 mTorr for 45 sec after cleaning the chamber for 5 min under the same conditions.
Immerse the chip in an ethanolic thiol solution consisting of a 3:1 ratio of SH-(CH2)8-EG3-OH and either SH-(CH2)11-EG3-NH2 or SH-(CH2)11-EG3-COOH overnight to form a self-assembled monolayer (SAM).
Rinse the chip with ethanol.
Dry the chip with nitrogen gas.
Functionalize a commercial bare gold chip with the SAM as described in Section 2.
Mix 133 mM EDC with 33 mM NHS in distilled deionized water (DDW) at a 1:1 ratio.
Incubate the mixture for 10 minutes to activate carboxyl groups on the surface of an SPC-based SAM.
Conjugate the activated carboxyl group with the antibody/ligand of interest using a flow rate of 30 µl/min for 300 seconds.
Prepare ligands in pH 6 phosphate buffer.
Flow 0.1 M ethanolamine in PBS through the system at a rate of 30 µl/min for 300 seconds to deactivate any remaining active sites.
Introduce the analyte of interest into the system using a flow rate of 100 µl/min across various concentrations.
Use kinetic analysis software to calculate kinetic rate constants from the data collected.
If non-specific binding is problematic, increase the ratio of SPO to SPC or SPN.
Koehler illuminate the sample with a 100 W Halogen lamp.
Place a long pass filter (typically 593 nm cutoff) in the light path to eliminate wavelengths not contributing to resonance shift.
Use an inverted microscope equipped with a 40X oil immersion objective (1.4 NA) and a thermoelectrically cooled 16-bit CCD camera for LSPRi data collection.
Place a beam splitter at the output port of the microscope to obtain imagery and spectra simultaneously.
Set the temperature-controlled microscope stage to 37 °C and equilibrate it for 4 hours before use.
Regulate CO2 concentration at 5% and humidity at 95% using an incubation assembly on the microscope.
Functionalize the LSPR chip as described in Section 2 with optimal two-component SAM ratios determined from SPR experiments.
Place the LSPR chip on an aluminum bottom piece.
Sandwich the chip between the bottom piece, a silicone gasket, and a clear plastic top piece.
Clamp the assembly using 4 screws.
Prepare a 1:1 mixture of 133 mM EDC and 33 mM NHS in DDW to activate carboxyl groups of SPC thiol component.
Drop coat the chip with 300 µl of the activated solution.
Wait for 10 min and manually rinse the surface with 10 mM PBS.
Conjugate the activated carboxyl group with ligand by drop coating 300 µl of ligand solution.
Wait for 30 min and manually rinse with 10 mM PBS.
Drop coat 300 µl of 0.1 M ethanolamine in PBS to minimize nonspecific binding.
Wait for 10 min and wash the ethanolamine with PBS containing 0.005% Tween 20 (PBS-T20).
Place a quartz piece above the chip to reduce fluctuations related to changing meniscus.
Keep the chip wet with PBS-T20 buffer while mounting on microscope.
Firmly place the LSPR chip assembly into the heated stage sample holder.
Attach microfluidic tubing.
Attach microfluidics tubing to the assembly.
Flow buffer or serum-free media until a steady state is reached.
Allow the assembly and microscope to equilibrate for at least 2 hours.
Align the chip using joystick so that the central array is aligned with the fiber optic for spectroscopy.
Take spectroscopic data using a spectrometer and spectral analysis software.
Keep arrays in focus throughout the experiment by using software autofocus or Zeiss Definite Focus.
Functionalize nanostructures with c-myc peptide.
Culture hybridoma cells in complete growth medium with 10% FBS and 1% antibiotic at 37 °C under 5% CO2.
Maintain a cell density of 4 × 10^5 cells/ml.
Pellet cells from the T75 flask by centrifugation for secretion studies.
Wash cells twice with RPMI-1640 serum-free media to remove secreted antibodies.
Adjust cell density to 4 × 10^6 cells/ml after washing.
Test harvested cells for viability before introducing them onto LSPR chips.
Introduce 50 μl of cell solution manually onto LSPR chips with a micropipette.
Allow cells to adhere to the surface of the LSPR chips for a few minutes.
Wash away remaining cells in solution with fresh SFM using the microfluidic perfusion system.
Select LSPR arrays for imaging which are close, within 10 μm, but not overlapping with the cells.
Introduce cell culture media without antibodies present for baseline measurement.
Introduce cell culture media with antibodies present to measure antibody presence.
Introduce cell culture media with antibodies and a saturating concentration of c-myc peptide to block binding sites.
Calibrate sensors at the end of each run with a saturating solution of anti-c-myc antibodies (250 nM).
Correct drift in X and Y direction using image alignment software.
